chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a number of our companions, that Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him)
whenever he was distressed, he left the optional (prayer).
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam do with optional prayers when he was distressed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) in prioritizing spiritual presence over ritual volume, illustrating the Shia principle that voluntary acts (nafl) are flexible and can be omitted when they might detract from the quality of obligatory duties. It underscores the scholarly view that 'ihtimam' (deep preoccupation or distress) serves as a valid excuse for suspending supererogatory prayers, preserving the integrity of the heart's focus.
